raw_response:
I've farmed these 5 mu for 55 years. I'm 75 now, and my wife and I do the work alone. Our children are in Shijiazhuang — they send a little money now and then, but the farm must feed us and pay for itself. We don't have much cash, so I don't try new things. I do what has worked, and I watch what my neighbors do. If Li down the road tries something and it fails, I don't touch it.

For wheat, I sow about 25 jin of seed per mu in early October, right after National Day. This year I'm using saved seed — I bought fresh two years ago, and it's still fine. Before sowing I spread about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu. That's my base. In March when the wheat turns green, I topdress with about 30 jin of urea per mu. I know the extension people say you can use less, but three years ago I cut back and the yield dropped badly. I can't afford that risk at my age. I irrigate three times — winter water if the soil is dry, green-up water in March, and jointing water in April. The pump electricity is expensive now, but you can't skip jointing water or you lose half your yield. I spray herbicide once in spring if I see weeds. This year there are some chenopodium weeds in the east field, so I'll spray.

For maize, after wheat harvest in early June, the window is tight — sometimes only three or four days before the soil dries out. I hire Old Wang's small tractor to plow, costs me 30 yuan per mu. I buy hybrid seed, about 6 jin per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 60 jin per mu. If the wheat yield was good and I have a little cash left, I'll side-dress with urea at the big trumpet stage, about 20 jin per mu. Maize doesn't need much irrigation if the summer rains come — maybe once at tasseling, or twice if July is dry like two years ago. I don't spray maize unless I see armyworms. Last year I didn't spray and it was fine, so I'll save the money.

I expect about 700 jin of wheat per mu and about 800 jin of maize if the weather is normal. I need to keep my spending around 2,000 yuan for the year. Last year fertilizer prices were high, so this year I'm using a little less compound to save money, but I'm keeping the urea. I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad harvest and have no grain in the bin. My neighbor Li tried some new slow-release fertilizer and said it was good, but it costs too much for a small farm like mine. At my age, stability matters more than trying to get a few extra jin.
